subproblem.title: Translates of integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^P: τ_vA is integer multiplicity, with translated action and translated measure
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) have an integer multiplicity representation R_A = (M, θ, ξ) (IMRep univ n with R_A.Represents A), and let v ∈ ℝ^P. Then there are A^v ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an integer multiplicity representation R^v (IMRep univ n) with R^v.Represents A^v such that (a) currentEval A^v φ = currentEval A (y ↦ φ(y + v)) for every n-form φ : ℝ^P → Λ^n(ℝ^P), whether or not φ is a test form, and (b) R^v.measure(C) = R_A.measure((y ↦ y + v)⁻¹(C)) for every Borel set C ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (RA : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (v : Euclid P), RA.Represents A → ∃ (Av : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Rv : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), Rv.Represents Av ∧ (∀ φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, currentEval Av φ = currentEval A (fun y => φ (y + v))) ∧ ∀ C : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet C → Rv.measure C = RA.measure ((fun y => y + v) ⁻¹' C)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent-supplied proof of face_currents (translates of integer multiplicity currents), with every IMRep field written out.
Accepted result used: Submission.dtc_imrep_current (every IMRep in U represents some current in U). It is a dependency of the ancestor minimality_transfer and is cited here by its exact Lean name.
Notation:
- H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^P = Euclid P;
- (M, θ, ξ) := (RA.carrier, RA.mult, RA.orient);
- e(x) := x − v and M' := e⁻¹(M) = {x : x − v ∈ M} = M + v;
- blowUpMap z ρ (y) = ρ⁻¹(y − z), the SimonGMT blow-up map.

1. (Translation preserves H^n.) μHE[n] on ℝ^P is translation invariant: Mathlib has the instance IsAddRightInvariant for μHE[d] in Mathlib/Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean. So e is measure preserving from H^n to H^n (measurePreserving_sub_right). Also e is a measurable equivalence (MeasurableEquiv.subRight v), hence a measurable embedding. Consequently:
 (i) H^n(e⁻¹(S)) = H^n(S) for every set S ⊆ ℝ^P, measurable or not (MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage_equiv);
 (ii) for every set S, every f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] and every F : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫⁻_{e⁻¹(S)} f(e(x)) dH^n(x) = ∫⁻_S f dH^n and ∫_{e⁻¹(S)} F(e(x)) dH^n(x) = ∫_S F dH^n (MeasurePreserving.setLIntegral_comp_preimage_emb, MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb);
 (iii) e is measure preserving from H^n⌞M' to H^n⌞M (MeasurePreserving.restrict_preimage; M is Borel by RA.measurableSet_carrier, and M' = e⁻¹(M)).

2. (Blow-up images.) For all x ∈ ℝ^P and ρ ∈ ℝ, blowUpMap x ρ '' M' = blowUpMap (x − v) ρ '' M:
 - if y ∈ M', then y − v ∈ M and ρ⁻¹(y − x) = ρ⁻¹((y − v) − (x − v));
 - if y ∈ M, then y + v ∈ M' and ρ⁻¹(y − (x − v)) = ρ⁻¹((y + v) − x).
 SimonGMT's HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N z Q means: finrank Q = n, and ∫_{blowUpMap z ρ '' N} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as ρ → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). It depends on (N, z) only through the sets blowUpMap z ρ '' N. Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (x − v) Q implies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q, with the same dimension condition and the same functions of ρ.

3. (The translated triple.) Let R^v := (M', θ', ξ') with θ'(x) := θ(x − v) and ξ'(x) := ξ(x − v). We check the IMRep fields.
 (a) M' = e⁻¹(M) is Borel (e is measurable and M is Borel), and M' ⊆ ℝ^P.
 (b) M' is countably n-rectifiable. By RA.rectifiable, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with H^n(M₀) = 0 and each F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^P Lipschitz with some constant K_j. Put M₀' := e⁻¹(M₀) and F_j'(z) := F_j(z) + v.
  - H^n(M₀') = H^n(M₀) = 0 by 1(i).
  - F_j' is Lipschitz with constant K_j: it is the sum of F_j and a constant map (LipschitzWith.add with LipschitzWith.const).
  - If x ∈ M', then x − v ∈ M. Either x − v ∈ M₀, so x ∈ M₀', or x − v = F_j(z) for some j and z, so x = F_j'(z).
  Hence M' ⊆ M₀' ∪ ⋃_j range F_j'.
 (c) θ' = θ ∘ e is measurable. For x ∈ M' we have x − v ∈ M, so θ'(x) = θ(x − v) > 0 by RA.mult_pos.
 (d) Local integrability. Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. K_v := {y : y + v ∈ K} = {x − v : x ∈ K} is compact, as the image of K under the continuous map x ↦ x − v. Also M' ∩ K = e⁻¹(M ∩ K_v). By 1(ii), ∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ'(x) dH^n(x) = ∫⁻_{e⁻¹(M∩K_v)} θ(e(x)) dH^n(x) = ∫⁻_{M∩K_v} θ dH^n, which is finite by RA.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set K_v ⊆ ℝ^P.
 (e) ξ' = ξ ∘ e is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M'. Indeed, ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M (RA.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), and e is measure preserving from H^n⌞M' to H^n⌞M by 1(iii) (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_measurePreserving).
 (f) Orientations. By RA.orients, for H^n⌞M-a.e. y there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q. A measure-preserving map is quasi-measure-preserving, so this a.e. property pulls back along e (QuasiMeasurePreserving.ae): for H^n⌞M'-a.e. x it holds at y = x − v. For such x and Q, step 2 gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q, and ξ'(x) = ξ(x − v) is a unit orientation of Q.
 Hence R^v is an IMRep of dimension n in ℝ^P.

4. (The current.) By Submission.dtc_imrep_current with U = ℝ^P, there is A^v ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with R^v.Represents A^v.

5. (Translation preserves test forms.) Let φ be a test form (C^∞ with compact support) and u ∈ ℝ^P. Then φ(· + u) is a test form:
 - it is smooth, as the composition of φ with the smooth map y ↦ y + u;
 - it equals φ ∘ h for the homeomorphism h(y) = y + u (Homeomorph.addRight u), so it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph).
 Applying this with u := −v: if φ(· + v) is a test form, then so is φ = (φ(· + v))(· − v).

6. (Proof of (a).) Let φ be an n-form.
 Case 1: φ is a test form. Then φ(· + v) is a test form by step 5, and both have tsupport ⊆ ℝ^P. By the definition of currentEval, currentEval A^v φ = A^v(φ) and currentEval A (φ(· + v)) = A(φ(· + v)). Now A^v(φ) = R^v.action(φ) = ∫_{M'} θ(x − v)·ξ(x − v)(φ(x)) dH^n(x). Since φ(x) = φ((x − v) + v), the integrand is G(e(x)) with G(y) := θ(y)·ξ(y)(φ(y + v)). By 1(ii) the integral equals ∫_M G dH^n = R_A.action(φ(· + v)), which is A(φ(· + v)) because R_A represents A.
 Case 2: φ is not a test form. Then φ(· + v) is not a test form either (step 5, contrapositive), so both sides of (a) are 0 by the definition of currentEval.

7. (Proof of (b).) Let C be Borel. Then C_v := (y ↦ y + v)⁻¹(C) is Borel. IMRep.measure is the withDensity of the multiplicity over H^n⌞carrier, so withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict give R^v.measure(C) = ∫⁻_{C∩M'} θ(x − v) dH^n(x). Now C ∩ M' = e⁻¹(C_v ∩ M), so by 1(ii) this equals ∫⁻_{C_v∩M} θ dH^n. By withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict again, that is R_A.measure(C_v) = R_A.measure((y ↦ y + v)⁻¹(C)). ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ x − v is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence of μHE[n] (translation invariance). This gives H^n(e⁻¹S) = H^n(S) for all S, change of variables on preimages, and measure preservation from H^n⌞(M + v) to H^n⌞M.
blowUpMap x ρ '' (M + v) = blowUpMap (x − v) ρ '' M, so approximate tangent planes of M at x − v are approximate tangent planes of M + v at x.

R^v = (M + v, θ(· − v), ξ(· − v)) satisfies every IMRep field (Borel, rectifiable via F_j + v, positive and locally integrable multiplicity, measurable orientation, a.e. orientation pulled back along e). Submission.dtc_imrep_current then gives A^v represented by R^v.

Test forms are invariant under translation. For test φ, change of variables gives R^v.action φ = R_A.action φ(· + v), i.e. (a); for non-test φ both currentEvals are 0. The same change of variables gives R^v.measure C = R_A.measure(C − v), i.e. (b).

subproblem.title: One face current: the product of the closed box Q_r(f) with the translate τ_wY is integer multiplicity, with mass (2r)^k μ_Y(ℝ^P) and the face action
subproblem.statement: Let P, k, m', n' ∈ ℕ with m' > 0 and h : n' = k + m'. Let f : Fin k → ℝ^P be orthonormal with span F := span{f_1, …, f_k}, and let w ∈ F^⊥. Let Y ∈ 𝒟_{m'}(ℝ^P) have an integer multiplicity representation R_Y (IMRep univ m', R_Y.Represents Y) whose measure is carried by F^⊥, i.e. R_Y.measure(ℝ^P ∖ F^⊥) = 0. Let r > 0, Q := {s ∈ F : |⟨f_c, s⟩| ≤ r for all c} and H^k := μHE[k]. Then there is an integer multiplicity current B ∈ 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P) with mass M(B) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k)·R_Y.measure(ℝ^P) such that, for every map flat : Λ^{n'} → Λ^{m'} with flat α v = α(Fin.append f v ∘ Fin.cast h) for all α and v, and every test n'-form ω, B(ω) = ∫_Q currentEval Y (y ↦ flat(ω(s + w + y))) dH^k(s). (B is [[Q]] ×_f τ_wY.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k m' n' : ℕ) (f : Fin k → Euclid P) (h : n' = k + m') (w : Euclid P) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m') (RY : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m') (r : ℝ), 0 < m' → Orthonormal ℝ f → w ∈ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range f))ᗮ → RY.Represents Y → RY.measure ((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range f))ᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 → 0 < r → ∃ B : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n', IsIntegerMultiplicity B ∧ B.mass = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * r) ^ k) * RY.measure univ ∧ ∀ flat : Covector (Euclid P) n' → Covector (Euclid P) m', (∀ (α : Covector (Euclid P) n') (v : Fin m' → Euclid P), flat α v = α (Fin.append f v ∘ Fin.cast h)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n', B ω = ∫ s in {s | s ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range f) ∧ ∀ c, |inner ℝ (f c) s| ≤ r}, currentEval Y (fun y => flat ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n') (s + w + y))) ∂μHE[k]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3–4 of the parent-supplied proof of face_currents, for one face. It is stated for a general orthonormal frame f (the parent uses f := g ∘ a.succAbove) and a general translation vector w ∈ F^⊥ (the parent uses w := ±r·g_a). The parent's Step 2 supplies w ∈ F^⊥ and the concentration of R_Y on F^⊥.
Results used:
- sibling translate_imrep (Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_fc_translate_imrep);
- Submission.idtp_fons_cs_sos_product_current and Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_frame_measure, dependencies of the parent face_currents, cited by exact Lean name;
- Submission.imrep_represents_massOn_eq_measure, a dependency of the ancestor minimality_transfer.
Notation: ω̂ := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n'); M(T) := T.mass, which for T ∈ 𝒟(ℝ^P) is T.massOn ℝ^P by definition.

1. (Translate.) Apply translate_imrep with n := m', A := Y, R_A := R_Y and v := w. It gives Y^w ∈ 𝒟_{m'}(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R^w with R^w.Represents Y^w and:
 (a) currentEval Y^w φ = currentEval Y (y ↦ φ(y + w)) for every m'-form φ;
 (b) R^w.measure(C) = R_Y.measure((y ↦ y + w)⁻¹(C)) for every Borel C.

2. (τ_wY is carried by F^⊥.) F^⊥ is closed (Submodule.isClosed_orthogonal), so ℝ^P ∖ F^⊥ is Borel. As w ∈ F^⊥ and F^⊥ is a subspace, y + w ∈ F^⊥ ⟺ y ∈ F^⊥ (Submodule.add_mem_iff_left). Hence (y ↦ y + w)⁻¹(ℝ^P ∖ F^⊥) = ℝ^P ∖ F^⊥, and 1(b) gives R^w.measure(ℝ^P ∖ F^⊥) = R_Y.measure(ℝ^P ∖ F^⊥) = 0.

3. (The box.) Q = F ∩ ⋂_c {s : |⟨f_c, s⟩| ≤ r}. F is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). Each set {s : |⟨f_c, s⟩| ≤ r} is closed, since s ↦ |⟨f_c, s⟩| is continuous. So Q is closed, hence Borel, and Q ⊆ F.

4. (The product.) Apply Submission.idtp_fons_cs_sos_product_current with (P, k, m', n'), the frame g := f, h, E := Q, A := Y^w and R_A := R^w. Its hypotheses hold: 0 < m', f orthonormal, Q Borel with Q ⊆ F (step 3), R^w.Represents Y^w (step 1), and R^w.measure(ℝ^P ∖ F^⊥) = 0 (step 2). It gives B ∈ 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R_B with R_B.Represents B such that:
 (i) R_B.measure(C) = ∫⁻_{t∈Q} R^w.measure((y ↦ t + y)⁻¹(C)) dH^k(t) for every Borel C;
 (ii) B(ω) = ∫_{t∈Q} currentEval Y^w (y ↦ flat(ω̂(t + y))) dH^k(t) for every flat with flat α v = α(Fin.append f v ∘ Fin.cast h) and every test n'-form ω.

5. (Integer multiplicity.) R_B represents B, so B is integer multiplicity.

6. (Action.) Fix such a flat and a test n'-form ω. For every t ∈ ℝ^P, apply 1(a) with φ := (y ↦ flat(ω̂(t + y))): currentEval Y^w φ = currentEval Y (y ↦ flat(ω̂(t + (y + w)))), and t + (y + w) = t + w + y. So the integrand in (ii) equals t ↦ currentEval Y (y ↦ flat(ω̂(t + w + y))) at every t, and B(ω) = ∫_Q currentEval Y (y ↦ flat(ω̂(s + w + y))) dH^k(s).

7. (Mass.) By Submission.imrep_represents_massOn_eq_measure (with U = W = ℝ^P, open, and R_B representing B), M(B) = B.massOn ℝ^P = R_B.measure(ℝ^P). By (i) with C = ℝ^P, whose preimages are all ℝ^P, R_B.measure(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_Q R^w.measure(ℝ^P) dH^k = R^w.measure(ℝ^P)·H^k(Q) (the lintegral of a constant over H^k⌞Q). By 1(b) with C = ℝ^P, R^w.measure(ℝ^P) = R_Y.measure(ℝ^P). By Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_frame_measure (ii) for the orthonormal frame f and r > 0, the closed box has H^k(Q) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k). Hence M(B) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k)·R_Y.measure(ℝ^P). ∎
proof_key_steps: translate_imrep gives τ_wY with an IMRep R^w, currentEval τ_wY φ = currentEval Y φ(· + w) for all φ, and R^w.measure C = R_Y.measure(C − w).
w ∈ F^⊥ makes F^⊥ invariant under + w, so R^w is carried by F^⊥. The box Q is closed and Q ⊆ F.
Submission.idtp_fons_cs_sos_product_current with frame f, E := Q and A := τ_wY gives B = [[Q]] ×_f τ_wY with an IMRep, the product measure formula and the product action.
Applied pointwise in t, the translation identity turns the action into ∫_Q currentEval Y (y ↦ flat(ω(s + w + y))) dH^k.

M(B) = R_B.measure(ℝ^P) = H^k(Q)·R_Y.measure(ℝ^P) = ofReal((2r)^k)·R_Y.measure(ℝ^P), by Submission.imrep_represents_massOn_eq_measure, the product measure formula and Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_frame_measure.
